💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rio Ngumoha is going to be a 'wow' player for Liverpool - and he indicated everyone exactly what he is already capable of in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United.
  • He made an outstanding assist then added a fine finish, and there is much more to come.
  • Ngumoha has only just turned 18 but he is already a game-changer, someone who gets people excited because he is so hard to stop when he is one-on-one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rio Ngumoha is going to be a 'wow' player for Liverpool - and he indicated everyone exactly what he is already capable of in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United.

He made an outstanding assist then added a fine finish, and there is much more to come. He plays without fear so he is going to score and make many more goals the same way.

Ngumoha has only just turned 18 but he is already a game-changer, someone who gets people excited because he is so hard to stop when he is one-on-one.

Of course he can frustrate you at times too, but that's what creative and explosive wingers like him do - and it's because he is so talented that everyone wants to see an end product from him every time he gets on the ball.

There were times against United when Ngumoha did not quite deliver, but he is still so young and I would much rather see players like him take too many touches - or try too many things and fail - than be afraid to try them in the first place.

So, if he runs out of play or runs into too many players at times, because teams are doubling up on him like United were, that just indicates how scared they are of him.

His ability means he occupies opposition players - Youri Tielemans was always backing up Diogo Dalot on his wing to try to help him out, but that just meant United were leaving someone else free.

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd.

Sometimes it is actually harder when you are playing out wide against 10 men because you don't get the same amount of space - United were not attacking the same way they would have done with 11, and they were sitting in more.

Recent findings suggest that yes, Ngumoha ran up the odd blind alley or got outnumbered but that is always going to happen. As he learns, and gets even better, his decision-making will improve too. He will know when to try to go past people or when to find that free man instead.

But he still highlighted all the bravery you want from a winger against United and, when you keep trying things the way he did, something is going to come off for you.

I look at Bradley Barcola in a similar way to Ngumoha - he can be frustrating but he tries things, and can be brilliant.

For Liverpool right now, one of the biggest positives is the competition they have in wide areas, with those two plus Victor Munoz and Cody Gakpo.

There are other areas of their squad, like left-back or central midfield, where that competition needs to improve, but I don't really worry about the wide attacking areas in the same way.

Sunday was only Ngumoha's second Premier League start of the season, and his first since the opening day.

He maybe only got his chance because Gakpo has a calf problem but, when everyone is fit, it is really exciting that they will all be thinking they have to play their best to push the manager and get in the team.

Andoni Iraola post-match interview - Liverpool v Man Utd.

Sources indicate that there were plenty of other positives for Liverpool, too. All in all, Sunday could not have gone much better for them.

United made a woeful start with poor concentration and mistakes which cost them but, from there, Liverpool saw the game out well.

Just because the opposition has a man sent off early on does not mean any kind of victory is a given, let alone a 4-0 win.

Look at how United's 11 men lost to City's 10 in the Manchester derby earlier this season - we've seen many times how good teams can frustrate a side with an extra player like that.

It definitely does not mean you are going to steamroller them, but Liverpool did that and made an abundance of chances to get even more goals.

Days like this are so vital for building belief in all their attacking players, especially because they were playing at home, and against their big rivals.

Up until now, it had felt like Liverpool's better days this season had come on the road, but now the pressure and expectation is off them a bit - particularly if, like Ngumoha or Florian Wirtz, you have scored and played well.

Industry observers note that I know from experience that, the next time they go back to Anfield, they will be buzzing. You know that the fans are already with you after you've scored against United, and you feel the love a little bit more.

This is the start of a big week for Liverpool and Iraola will probably make changes against Club Brugge in Belgium on Wednesday, knowing how difficult Sunday's Merseyside derby will be.

Everton is always a tough game but I think Liverpool will enjoy their trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium, and the confidence they will have after beating United will mean they can go there with a really positive mindset.

Danny Murphy was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

Wirtz had a 'substantial game, and he shone'.

#139317. Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1670 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1670 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov.
  • According to recent reports, voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, flew past Neptune.
  • "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a major milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth, something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary.

According to recent reports, voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, flew past Neptune. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space.

"I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. What an incredible milestone," Voyager project scientist Linda Spilker said during Thursday's event.

While this day and this week have been chock-full of excitement over the distance milestone, the Voyager mission team has been hard at work, as usual, keeping the two nearly 50-year-old spacecraft alive and functioning.

Unfortunately, as JPL spokesperson Raquel Villanueva shared at this celebration, on Saturday (Nov. 14), Voyager 1 stopped transmitting science and engineering data. The team has remained in contact with Voyager 1 while investigating the issue, and they are confident that they'll be able to solve it soon.

"We listen to each spacecraft every day," Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd told Space.com at the event. Regarding Voyager 1, "we have an anomaly that is not something unseen before," Dodd noted. "We do have a very strong carrier signal. We right now don't have a frame sync, so we're not getting the science or engineering data currently.".

"But if you recall," Dodd added, "one light-day is very far from us. [It takes] 24 hours to get the signal to the spacecraft, 24 hours for the signal to come down, so it takes two days to diagnose anything on the spacecraft … So we can't do anything fast, and the data rates are very low.".

Recent findings suggest that according to Dodd, this anomaly isn't a major cause for long-term concern. Rather, it's likely just part of the natural aging process for spacecraft.

"These spacecraft are old," she remarked. "All of us old people have our aches and pains, and you know, sometimes it takes longer to stretch out your muscles and remember things, and so we are in a realm where we're going to see more anomalies with Voyager just due to the distance and the age.".

"But we feel Voyager 1, although it's not sending us the telemetry data, it's pointed at the Earth. It's sending us a strong carrier signal, and I'm confident that it won't be too long, and it will send us data back.".

In a recent development, and, for anyone curious how Voyager 1's slower twin Voyager 2 is faring, Dodd shared that it is doing very well on its own journey through interstellar space. "Voyager 2 is very healthy. It's continuing its mission. It has three scientific instruments on it," she told Space.com.

"Each spacecraft is basically setting a record every day for longevity or distance," Dodd added about the twin probes.

Industry observers note that despite the communications anomaly — and even though most of the team had been up all night to confirm the one-light-day signal from Voyager 1 — the room was alive with excitement. The Voyagers have been flying for nearly 50 years on a mission expected to last just five years, so the team was beyond ready to celebrate.

Amidst the more technical updates about the mission and its current status out in interstellar space, the event included footage of Voyager light-day celebrations from around the world. From children cheering on Voyager to iconic landmarks lighting up gold in honor of the mission's Golden Record, the Voyager love echoed around the world in photos and videos. The footage of this international celebration was enough to move Nicky Fox, NASA's associate administrator for the Science Mission Directorate, nearly to tears.

"I actually thought I was going to start sobbing," Fox joked to Space.com after the media briefing. "I think just hearing children's voices and people saying 'We love you, Voyager,' 'Go Voyager' — it just was amazing.".

Industry observers note that and Fox and the mission team members weren't the only ones sharing their love for Voyager. NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins beamed down her own video message to the Voyager 1 spacecraft from the International Space Station, sharing in the celebration.

"Dear Voyager 1," Watkins said. "As an orbiting outpost just 250 miles [400 kilometers] above Earth, we often feel distant yet deeply connected to our home planet. The International Space Station has had crew continuously living off of the Earth for 26 years, seen hundreds of visitors from around the world, and enabled thousands of experiments to advance space exploration.

"While you have been traveling into the unknown for nearly half a century, helping pave our path, together, our two journeys tell a single story of exploration," she continued. "One remains close to home, and the other reaches ever outward. Voyager 1, you have been a beacon of light, a symbol of exploration, a seeker of truth, a carrier of hope, a brave explorer, traveling further than any human hand has ever reached. You represent the very best of what humanity has to offer.

"As you reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, the entire crew of Expedition 75 and people across the planet send you our admiration and our wishes for a safe and continued journey as you begin your post-one-light-day era. There are so many amazing milestones and discoveries to come. You have a universe ahead of you, and you carry with you our collective hopes and dreams. When we look up from Earth, we will always think of you as you continue forward into the great unknown. May you continue shining bright for all of us. Go Voyager 1!" Watkins stated, ending her message with a weightless backflip from aboard the station.

In concluding the media briefing, the mission team invited those in the room who, over the past 50 years (or more, with one person sharing their excitement having worked on Voyager before it was even called Voyager) have worked on the mission in one way or another, to stand up to a round of applause. With mission team members today ranging from those in their 20s to their 90s, the people behind this enduring mission span many generations.

According to recent reports, interestingly, Fox actually began her light-day celebrations earlier in the week. She, alongside writer/producer Ann Druyan — who was the wife of the late astronomer Carl Sagan, whose work helped create the mission's Golden Record and who took the now-famous "pale blue dot" Voyager image of Earth to the public — together lit up the Empire State Building gold.

In a recent development, "I was actually very privileged to flick the switch and turn on the Empire State Building lights on Tuesday evening [Nov. 17]," Fox, wearing golden Voyager-inspired nail polish crafted by her daughter, told Space.com. "That was just spectacular … I was there with Ann … we were both so giddy with the excitement of doing it … It was amazing. And then going up and standing underneath and seeing the tower was just really, really special.".

In a recent development, while the room lit up with excitement for Voyager's light-day milestone on Thursday, the team was also brimming with anticipation for what lies ahead. As Voyager hurtles toward another major milestone, turning 50 in 2027, it remains an active science mission, and the team remains hard at work to push the boundaries of exploration with these aging probes.

"Voyager right now — the two Voyagers — they're in an area of space that we've never been into. So every single bit of data that comes back is precious because it's unique," Fox said.

In a recent development, "Now we're in a region where the sun's influence is a lot different, and we're in this region where we can start to understand: What is it like out past our sun? What is it like in the space between the stars?" Voyager deputy project scientist Jamie Rankin told Space.com. "We're at a very exciting time of starting to connect what we know and what we've seen, living with this star [our sun] to what is out there.".

"What's next? Voyager is just going to keep on going. You know, people sometimes think, 'When's the mission going to end?' It's never going to end," Fox added to Space.com. "Even when we can no longer talk to Voyager, they're both going to keep going … So there's no end for the Voyager mission.".

According to recent reports, chelsea Gohd served as a Senior Writer for Space.com from 2018 to 2022 before returning in 2026, covering everything from climate change to planetary science and human spaceflight in both articles and on-camera in videos. With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. 'Our Super Bowl moment' - what can WSL learn from booming US league?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1639 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kansas City Current, who were formed in 2020, won this year's National Women's Soccer League championship.
  • Sarah Jones Simmer, chief operating officer of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL), could not wait for the championship game between Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current on Saturday night.
  • The NWSL showpiece was played out in front of a sellout crowd of more than 19,000 at Audi Field in Washington DC, with tickets retailing at more than $300 (Â£229).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kansas City Current, who were formed in 2020, won this year's National Women's Soccer League championship.

"It's turning into our Super Bowl moment.".

Sarah Jones Simmer, chief operating officer of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL), could not wait for the championship game between Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current on Saturday night.

The NWSL showpiece was played out in front of a sellout crowd of more than 19,000 at Audi Field in Washington DC, with tickets retailing at more than $300 (Â£229).

Ultimately, the Current triumphed 2-1 to clinch their first title, condemning Spirit to an unwanted record of three lost finals in a row.

Just a few hours earlier on this side of the Atlantic, Alexia Putellas, who last month was crowned the best player in the world for the third time at the Ballon d'Or ceremony, was scoring twice for London City against Crystal Palace in front of 4,000 people in Bromley.

Industry observers note that it is a totally unfair comparison. After all, a championship final is the type of jamboree the USA does particularly well.

Nevertheless, women's football is booming in America at the moment, with attendance figures at record highs, more franchises joining the league and club retail sales double those of 2025.

So what is behind the explosion in popularity?

And what can the Women's Super League learn from it?

The US is the most successful nation in women's international football.

The four-time World Cup winners (1991, 1999, 2015 and 2019) and five-time Olympic gold medallists, the nation of Mia Hamm, Alex Morgan and Megan Rapinoe, has a history of winning - and the domestic game is key.

"If anything, soccer is more seen as a women's sport [in the USA]," indicates broadcaster Jacqui Oatley, who currently commentates on the NWSL for ESPN.

"Women have won World Cups and Olympic Games - and the men have been nowhere near as successful.".

While teams in the United States became professional in 2001 - for WSL teams it was 2018 - the top flight has taken several different guises over the years.

The current NWSL kicked off in 2013 as an eight-team competition, and has since expanded to 16 franchises, with two more joining from 2028.

There is no relegation and Kansas City's victory on Saturday means the league has had eight different winners since its iteration.

As the below graph highlights, the ownership picture for these sides is far more varied than in the UK, with American sides much less dependent on their male counterparts.

According to recent reports, indeed, Kansas City are blazing a trail. Established in December 2020, unaffiliated to a men's side and backed by ambitious owners that include Brittany Mahomes - the wife of NFL quarterback Patrick Mahomes.

Winning the championship is the crowning achievement for an ambitious franchise and such success is something independent London City hope to emulate in the UK. They are four points from the WSL summit nearly halfway through the 2026-27 season.

Kansas City were also the first club to build a bespoke stadium solely for women's football and the demand for seats at their 11,500-seater CPKC Stadium is huge. Earlier this year, Brighton confirmed their own purpose-built venue, planned for 2030-31.

"I think our independence is a hallmark of the league," notes the NWSL's Jones Simmer.

"It is something we are very proud of. It allows us to invest in our own growth, prioritise the women's game and ensure resources are flowing to it.".

It is markedly different from the UK set-up, where all WSL teams bar London City are, at least, affiliated and more often financially reliant on the men's side.

But that presents just as much of an opportunity, according to Jones Simmer.

"I know Nikki [Doucet, chief executive of the WSL] and I admire what she is building," she says.

"There's a really unique opportunity to build on the legacy of these 100-year-old men's clubs that are household names, to build women's brands that embrace the legacy but also have their own identity.".

Bespoke women's football stadiums? Why US sides are making the move.

Brighton proposal Europe's first purpose-built Â£80m women's stadium.

Washington Spirit's Trinity Rodman benefited from a NWSL decision in December 2025 to lift the league's salary cap for a 'High Impact Player'.

Fans of both the NWSL and the WSL are spoiled when it comes to talent.

Most of the US national team play their club football at home, with the likes of Trinity Rodman, Mallory Swanson and Rose Lavelle household names.

International stars such as Malawi's Temwa Chawinga at Kansas City, who came 10th in the 2026 Ballon d'Or rankings, and former Chelsea striker Sam Kerr further enhance the league's quality.

Industry observers note that "Where it starts is the product on the pitch," says Jones Simmer. "The quality of football has to be incredible and we have the best players in the world.

"And they are incredibly engaging with our fans. For so many supporters, their entry point to the league is they care about a particular player.".

Provided the standard of competition is present, Jones Simmer indicates fans will return - and her confidence is backed up by the numbers.

In 2026, the average gate for an NWSL match has been more than 11,000 - only Arsenal in the WSL consistently receive a higher attendance than that, albeit the US is almost five times more populous than the UK.

On Thursday, the final few tickets for the NWSL's showpiece were retailing at $300 on ticket site Viagogo, with Jones Simmer suggesting resale tickets could be purchased at six times market value in advance of the match.

As London City and Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang put it: "The answer could not be clearer that there is an audience for the women's game.".

"It's our job to hook fans by making sure they have a great experience watching a game in a venue and that's about the quality of the product," Jones Simmer adds.

"Once folks have that experience, it's a really easy yes to tune in again.".

Families v loyal fans - women's football's attendance dilemma.

Sources indicate that not that quality is an matter in the WSL where high-class footballers abound. Take Putellas, goal machine Khadija Shaw and most of England's double European Championship-winning squad for example.

American stars such as Alyssa Thompson and Naomi Girma at Chelsea, and Manchester City's Sam Coffey, have also swapped the US for the WSL in the past two years.

Broadcaster Oatley, who has been covering women's football since the 2005 World Cup, is keen for such players to be more visible off the pitch.

"I would love to see WSL players on mainstream TV shows, podcasts, social media platforms, not just on women's football programmes where the audience already knows everything about them," she states.

"It would not be for everyone, but for those who are comfortable, who have the biggest personalities, I think we could use that much more to grow our audience.".

Oatley has been covering NWSL games for the past four seasons and she believes US clubs have mastered putting on events.

"When you're trying to promote a product in sport, you can't guarantee the team is going to play well and win," she says.

"But you can ensure the people who come to the game have a great experience.

According to recent reports, "I love the enthusiasm, the positivity, the vibe of 'let's make this massive'. It's a brilliant experience.".

It is a balance the WSL wrestles with. With attendances plateauing this season, questions have arisen around its target audience and whether to market matches such as the north London derby between Tottenham and Arsenal as a rivalry or a family-friendly event.

Oatley's perspective is that it ought to be both, while recognising the different challenges in this country.

According to recent reports, "I didn't understand that criticism," she states, "because they weren't saying: 'Only come to this game if you're a family'. It was being promoted all round.

"I don't think it's one size fits all marketing wise - the main thing is awareness.".

The NWSL Fan Fest at The Wharf in Washington DC was part of a series of events around the championship game on Saturday.

It is a challenge the NWSL has embraced, and seen attendances rise accordingly.

"We want to ensure that we provided a big enough tent where everyone can feel welcome and included, whether they're there for the rivalries and the competitive tactics, or they're experiencing it for the first time," notes Jones Simmer.

"To grow the sport, all fans need to be able to come to an NWSL game and have a great experience.".

This season, league finalists Current and Spirit played at a remarkable 17 different times between them, reflecting the four timezones and vast nature of the USA.

It is all part of the country's sporting landscape, but given the WSL's continued conundrum about fixture scheduling, it is interesting that NWSL supporters manage to find the matches regardless.

"I have a lot of sympathy with schedulers because men's football got there first," Oatley states.

"Maybe the solution is deciding certain time slots are for women's football and sticking with them.".

It does not appear the growth in the NWSL will slow down any time soon.

The Women's World Cup in Brazil next summer will feature the USA as one of the favourites and women's soccer will feature at the Olympic Games in Los Angeles in 2028.

The US will also host the 2031 Women's World Cup.

"It is amazing how the NWSL is cracking into culture," Jones Simmer claims.

"We get excited about these catalytic opportunities to expand the community engagement, awareness and relevance of the NWSL.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the past few years, WIRED has tested nearly every major brand of essential oil diffuser.
  • Recent findings suggest that in fact, no brand even comes close to Pura's sheer breadth of available fragrances—with more than 150 options from massive names like Anthropologie, Nest, LAFCO, Brooklyn Candle Organization, Studio McGee, and more.
  • Industry observers note that but, it's a luxury you'll pay for.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the past few years, WIRED has tested nearly every major brand of essential oil diffuser. Pura’s been our top nebulizer-style device (these work by blowing air through oil) for years due to its ease of use and sprawling library of high-end scents.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, no brand even comes close to Pura's sheer breadth of available fragrances—with more than 150 options from massive names like Anthropologie, Nest, LAFCO, Brooklyn Candle Organization, Studio McGee, and more. Pura even has special seasonal collabs, like this month’s Nutcracker-inspired scents from the Fresh York City Ballet. These diffusers are also highly convenient to use in that you can control them from your phone via an app (the Home, Plus, and Car also have buttons on the actual devices).

Industry observers note that but, it's a luxury you'll pay for. If you own a Pura or have seen it in stores, you already know the scents aren't cheap; single cartridges range from $14 for Pura’s house line all the way up to $21 for name brands like Thymes and Votivo. (The prices displayed on Pura's website look lower, but that's only if you buy a recurring subscription—make sure you note the one-time purchase price.).

Cartridges can last for a month or more in the Pura Mini, but in a larger diffuser like the Pura Plus, they may only last a couple of weeks. That's why the best time to stock up on scents for the year is during a sale, like Pura’s Cyber Week event. Right now through December 6, all fragrances are 20 percent off, and all diffusers are 30 percent off.

Pura's diffuser lineup isn't perfect, but neither are any of the diffusers we've tried from any brand. Diffusers can be loud or messy, take up a lot of space, or have an uninspiring line of scents. Pura's Mini and Car models are worthwhile yet quirky (though I can't recommend the Plus), but the Home has given me no issues in six months of testing.

Industry observers note that if you're in the market for a Pura diffuser, our top pick for most people is the newly introduced Pura Home. The first Pura I ever owned was the 3 model, and I've also had the 4, but the 5 (rebranded “Home”) improves on just about everything, with dual-band (2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz) Wi-Fi compatibility; faster diffusion; control buttons on the device itself; and even a new way to load cartridges, where you can slide out the bottom portion (which is flat to sit on a surface), seat the scents, and click it into place. QR codes on the cartridges inform your app which scents they are and when they were loaded, so it can, in turn, remind you when it's time to replace them. I also like that this model is totally silent.

In a recent development, I also recommend the oval-shaped Mini—I have one in my office right now. Though you can only control it via Pura's app, scents last for over a month, and it does a great job at scenting a smaller space like a bedroom. My unit makes a high-pitched ringing noise, almost like an ultrasonic pest repellent, which is annoying, but Pura's customer service will likely replace yours if this happens to you.

It has been revealed that there’s also the Pura Car, whose refills I will be purchasing during this sale (MSRP averages $21 apiece, and the four-week run time has been roughly accurate in my experience). Online reviews of this device are mixed, but I love mine. If you’re a parent, having Pura scents to inhale instead of old, spilled food and stinky soccer cleats is 100 percent worth the spend. Buy one for a mom you know, but only if she has USB charging ports in her car—it needs to be plugged in most of the time, as it doesn’t hold a charge for very long.

Also on sale for 20 percent off is Pura's fun fresh Advent calendar, which features a Pura Home diffuser and 12 best-selling scents, most of which I have tried and can vouch for being options most people would enjoy.

Another Pura Cyber Week deal: Spend $50, and get 50 percent off the Pura Plus diffuser for large spaces, which has an MSRP of $80. I didn’t have the best of luck with the two Plus devices I went through—both eventually developed a loud buzzing noise. (Note that Pura will send you a replacement if this happens to you.) Additionally, unlike the Puras that sit flush to the outlet, this one is a cylinder that sits apart and must be plugged in at all times. It also makes an audible, fixed “shhhhhhh” noise as it’s long as it’s on (unlike the more intermittent noise emitted by competitors). However, it did do a great job of scenting a high-ceilinged room on the first floor of my house.

SpaceX Dragon cargo capsule returns to Earth from the ISS

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (431 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SpaceX's 35th Dragon cargo mission has come home to Earth.
  • Recent findings suggest that the robotic Dragon capsule undocked from the International Space Station (ISS) on Friday (Nov.
  • The freighter made its way Earthward over the next 29 hours, ultimately splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX's 35th Dragon cargo mission has come home to Earth.

Recent findings suggest that the robotic Dragon capsule undocked from the International Space Station (ISS) on Friday (Nov. 20) at 12:05 p.m. EST (1705 GMT), while the duo were flying 260 miles (418 kilometers) above western China.

The freighter made its way Earthward over the next 29 hours, ultimately splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov. 21) at 5:03 p.m. EST (2155 GMT).

The Dragon rolled out Oct. 13, on a mission called CRS-35 because it was the 35th that SpaceX has flown for NASA's Commercial Resupply Services program.

The capsule arrived at the ISS on Oct. 15, delivering more than 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of food, scientific gear and other supplies to the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. It brought a lot of stuff down to Earth, too.

"Thousands of pounds of cargo are returning from the space station, including research samples that could advance future space exploration and improve life on Earth," NASA officials wrote in an revision on Tuesday (Nov. 17).

"The returning research includes a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct scientists used to study vascular aging and cardiovascular disease in space and on Earth," they added.

Dragon is the only cargo craft flying today that's capable of making such downward deliveries. The others — Northrop Grumman's Cygnus, Russia's Progress vehicle and Japan's HTV-X — are all expendable and burn up in Earth's atmosphere to wrap up their first and only spaceflight.

Editor's note: This story was updated at 12:20 p.m. ET on Nov. 20 with news of successful undocking, then again at 8:55 p.m. ET on Nov. 21 with news of splashdown.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd.

"Sacked in the morning, you're getting sacked in the morning...".

Fourteen minutes in, arms folded, two goals down at Liverpool and with his Manchester United team reduced to 10 men, Mauricio Pochettino could not ignore the cruel taunts echoing around Anfield.

What on earth must Pochettino have been thinking as he stood at the edge of his technical area?

In distance terms, he was 3,800 miles from his last managerial assignment against Haiti in Cincinnati in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time.

In difficulty levels, it must have felt significantly further than that.

By the final whistle, as Liverpool's gleeful supporters alternated between singing about the notion of Pochettino's immediate dismissal, United "going down" and celebrating "Poch is at the wheel", the Argentine head coach would have been starting to understand the scale of the task he has taken on by quitting his United States job.

He had just watched United be dismantled 4-0 by their oldest rivals, with Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card and two quickfire goals soon after representing just about the worst possible start imaginable to his reign as manager.

His team sit 19th in the 20-team Premier League after 11 games, already 20 points behind leaders Arsenal.

"Animals of the grass, we like to smell it and feel it," was the memorable phrase Pochettino came out with during Friday's pre-match media conference, explaining how he has missed the day-to-day nature of club football.

Listen to former United skipper Roy Keane's post-match summary of the loss on Sky Sports and a very different smell comes to mind.

For the record, it was the joint-worst result for any newly introduced United boss, matching the 4-0 loss Lal Hilditch suffered against Bolton in October 1926.

Hilditch lasted 30 games and never managed another team.

Pochettino endures nightmare start as Man Utd lose to Liverpool.

The red card that changed Liverpool-Man Utd: correct call?

Yoro sees red as Ngumoha shines - Liverpool v Man Utd player ratings.

Liverpool run riot for Pochettinoâs nightmare debut.

Keane is not one for holding back, so his response to his old side's latest setback was predictable.

Industry observers note that "Fans are applauding the players [at the end]. Applauding what? Applauding rubbish," he mentioned. "When do the players take responsibility for some of the decision-making?".

There were enough images of chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox broadcast during the game by Sky Sports to suggest there is a wider debate to be had about the quality of the players at Pochettino's disposal.

Recent findings suggest that on Friday, Berrada noted this season's squad was "fundamentally better" than the one which finished third last season. Few would agree with that, and presumably Keane is among the group who would challenge Berrada's assertion.

Pochettino, 54, shed tears of emotion when he explained his difficulty in deciding to quit the United States job and take up an opportunity at a club he has flirted with for the best part of a decade but, only now, has been given the chance to coach.

It was easy to imagine him being reduced to tears again as Sunday's debacle unfolded, a nightmare afternoon in Liverpool coming at the end of a chaotic week of travel.

He arrived to begin his new role as United head coach on Wednesday after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract.

It has been revealed that the USA beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati in his final game in charge on Tuesday, with Pochettino flying directly to Manchester on a private jet after the game. He landed at about 11:30 GMT before heading to the club's Carrington training ground - and his feet have barely touched the floor since.

Mauricio Pochettino gives his post-match verdict on Liverpool v Man Utd.

Pochettino was bullish when speaking to the media after this 4-0 defeat.

Although he began his first answer by saying he went to referee Sam Barrott after the final whistle to "present his respect", he became increasingly more forceful in his view Leny Yoro should not have been sent off.

After dismissing the sorry statistic that United have conceded 19 goals in their latest six games, because he didn't want to talk about results and performances that occurred before he replaced Michael Carrick, he then used Yoro's red card as the prism through which his side's entire performance at Anfield should be judged.

In a recent development, "What I learned from my players [today] is that they like to fight. They are committed with the team, with the club, and of course they want to win games," Pochettino mentioned.

It has been revealed that "Today we made an unbelievable effort. Today was a test. After eight minutes, 10 men, red card, concede the goal in this action. Do you think that is easy?

"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more.".

Man Utd shouldn't worry about relegation, yet - Young.

Industry observers note that it is a basic truth that Pochettino won six games this season as United States boss, twice as many as United have managed in 16 matches across all competitions. His newly introduced team have kept one clean sheet, against Azerbaijanis Sabah FK in the Champions League in September.

Pochettino's biggest selection call was to alter his defence by handing Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in almost 12 months.

It was a De Ligt misread of a bouncing ball that led to Yoro having to decide whether to foul Alexander Isak before he entered the penalty area.

Sources indicate that "It was clearly a foul and he was clearly the last man," stated home boss Andoni Iraola, giving his reading from a Liverpool perspective. "Will he score? We will never know.".

Pochettino had a different opinion.

"If you go a minute and a half before, [Jeremy] Jacquet and [Bryan] Mbeumo and compare it..." he mentioned, suggesting his team should have been awarded an earlier penalty.

"Yes, it's painful because it's 4-0. But for us to play 80 minutes with 10 men is unfair. We need to be critical but the action of Liverpool [player] was also a mistake, no? But we were punished and they were not. That is the truth.".

Pochettino takes his team, and his grievance, to Lisbon on Wednesday for a Champions League encounter with Sporting.

According to recent reports, after that, it is Brentford, Newcastle and Coventry in the Premier League. This, to an extent, was a game United and their fans, and even Keane probably, expected little from.

If they are still in the relegation zone after Coventry have left Old Trafford on 5 December, United really are in trouble.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that ATEEZ‘s GOLDEN HOUR: Part.6 puts K-pop back in a familiar spot — No. 1 on the all-genre Billboard 200 chart. It’s the 27th album or EP by a K-pop act to reach No. 1 on Billboard’s flagship albums chart in just over eight years. The first was BTS’ Love Yourself: Tear, back in June 2018.

This is the fifth K-pop album or EP to top Billboard 200 in 2026, which ties 2023 as the year with the most K-pop leaders.

According to recent reports, here’s another fun fact: ATEEZ’s EP opened with 195,000 equivalent album units earned in the United States. That’s the highest one-week total for any release (from any genre) since another K-Pop act, Stray Kids, opened with 369,000 equivalent album units of This & That on the chart dated Aug. 22.

Sources indicate that stray Kids has amassed nine No. 1 titles on the Billboard 200, which puts the group out front among K-pop acts. BTS is second, with seven No. 1 titles. ATEEZ is next in line with four No. 1s. SuperM, BLACKPINK, TOMORROW X TOGETHER, NewJeans, TWICE and ENHYPEN have all notched one No. 1 to date. In addition, one multi-artist K-pop soundtrack, KPop Demon Hunters, has reached No. 1.

BLACKPINK was the first female K-pop act to land a No. 1 album on the Billboard 200. They scored with Born Pink in 2022. They were followed by NewJeans and TWICE.

Sources indicate that K-pop groups tend to be large ensembles. TWICE has nine members, one more than Stray Kids and ATEEZ. BTS has seven members, as did SuperM, which went on hiatus in mid-2021. ENHYPEN has six members. TOMORROW X TOGETHER and NewJeans each have five members. BLACKPINK has four members. To date, no K-pop solo artists, duos or trios have topped the Billboard 200.

There have been multiple No. 1 albums on the Billboard 200 by K-pop acts in every year since 2018 except for 2021, when there were none.

Here’s a list of all K-pop albums to top the Billboard 200. They are listed in chronological order.

Date Hit No. 1: September 8, 2018.

It has been revealed that date Hit No. 1:  April 27, 2019.

Singles: “Boy with Luv,” “Make It Right”.

Date Hit No. 1: October 19, 2019.

Single: “Yet to Come (The Most Beautiful Moment)”.

Singles: “Pink Venom,” “Shut Down”.

Singles: “Super Shy,” “Cool With You,” “ETA”.

Singles: “I Got You,” “One Spark”.

Singles: “Takedown” (Twice version), “Golden” and “How It’s Done” (HUNTR/X: EJAE, Audrey Nuna & REI AMI).

Industry observers note that notes: The album returned to No. 1 in the problem dated Oct. 11, making it the first K-pop album to log two or more weeks at No. 1.

It has been revealed that date Hit No. 1: April 4, 2026Singles: “Swim,” “Hooligan,” “Normal”Notes: The album held at No. 1 on the chart dated April 11, becoming the first K-pop album to spend two consecutive weeks on top. It held at No. 1 again on the chart dated April 18, becoming the first K-pop album to spend three or more weeks on top.

#139304. Tech Report: Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1078 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1078 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every one of 212 plant-based foods and drinks tested in a new study contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, raising questions about the potential health effects of regularly consuming these products.
  • Researchers examined a wide selection of vegetarian and vegan products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives and dairy substitutes.
  • Mycotoxins are poisonous substances produced by certain fungi, including molds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every one of 212 plant-based foods and drinks tested in a new study contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, raising questions about the potential health effects of regularly consuming these products.

Researchers examined a wide selection of vegetarian and vegan products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives and dairy substitutes. They detected at least one of 19 mycotoxins in every product, and many contained multiple toxins.

Mycotoxins are poisonous substances produced by certain fungi, including molds. They can enter the food supply when agricultural crops become contaminated during growing, harvesting, or storage.

Industry observers note that the investigation was led by scientists at the University of Parma in Italy, with contributions from Cranfield University. The researchers analyzed 212 products, including plant-based meat alternatives (PMBAs) and plant-based beverages (PBBs). The selection covered foods commonly found on supermarket shelves, such as vegan burgers, vegetarian chicken pieces, vegan sausages, and oat, almond, and soy milk.

Although the findings highlight how widespread these naturally occurring contaminants can be, the researchers also identified an notable reassuring detail. Every product contained mycotoxin concentrations below recommended European Union guideline levels, which the team remarked reflected the high food quality standards maintained by the UK food industry.

Why Plant-Based Foods Can Contain Fungal Toxins.

Many of the ingredients used to manufacture plant-based foods are particularly susceptible to fungal contamination. Grains, legumes, and seeds can encounter mold in fields or storage facilities, creating opportunities for mycotoxins to develop before the ingredients reach food manufacturers.

According to recent reports, unlike bacteria or viruses, mycotoxins are chemical substances produced by certain fungi. Their presence in food does not necessarily mean the product contains living mold, and detecting a toxin does not automatically mean the food is unsafe. The potential health risk depends on factors such as the type of toxin, its concentration, and how much a person consumes over time.

Sources indicate that this distinction is especially important for people who eat plant-based products frequently. Someone whose diet regularly includes meat substitutes, dairy alternatives, grains, and legumes may encounter these substances through several different foods rather than a single source.

Could Repeated Exposure Pose Health Risks?

While the concentrations detected in the UK products were below recommended EU guidelines, researchers say the potential effects of repeated exposure deserve closer attention.

Industry observers note that earlier studies have suggested that consuming small amounts of mycotoxins regularly may contribute to cumulative exposure and potentially increase health risks. In other words, assessing a single product may not provide a complete picture of a person's overall dietary exposure.

Eating one of these products occasionally is unlikely to cause problems based on the levels reported. However, a diet that relies heavily or exclusively on plant-based foods could involve repeated exposure to mycotoxins from numerous ingredients and products. Researchers say understanding the combined effects is important for evaluating possible long-term health consequences.

Recent findings suggest that the severity of mycotoxin exposure varies depending on the compounds involved and the amount consumed. At sufficiently high or harmful exposure levels, certain mycotoxins can damage the liver and kidneys, interfere with normal immune system function, and increase the risk of cancer.

The upcoming findings do not establish that the tested products cause these conditions. Instead, they provide information that scientists can use to estimate how much exposure consumers may receive through their diets and develop more accurate food safety risk assessments for the UK population.

Scientists Call for Better Monitoring of Plant-Based Ingredients.

Andrea Patriarca, Senior Lecturer in Mycology at Cranfield University, emphasized that mycotoxins are a natural part of the food environment and should not discourage people from eating a varied diet. Mycology is the branch of biology devoted to studying fungi, including molds and yeasts.

"Mycotoxins occur naturally in foods and cannot be completely avoided. As consumers, we should not be frightened or deterred from enjoying a variety of products.

Recent findings suggest that however, a significant concern arises when newly introduced foods enter the market, as there are right now no established regulations to monitor mycotoxins. We collaborate closely with various sectors in the food industry, from farmers to food companies, to help implement effective mycotoxin management integrated within food safety standards. The data from our research helps food safety organizations in assessing risks, particularly in complex multi-ingredient products.

We are at the moment collaborating with the University of Parma to evaluate the risks faced by the population based on different dietary habits. Our aim is to advise policymakers and raise awareness among vulnerable consumers.".

The researchers are particularly interested in how food safety monitoring can keep pace with the growing range of plant-based products. Foods made from multiple ingredients present additional challenges because each component may introduce different contaminants, making overall exposure more difficult to assess.

Industry observers note that their work also underscores the importance of monitoring raw materials throughout the food production process. Identifying and controlling contamination before ingredients are combined into finished products could help manufacturers manage potential risks more effectively.

What the Findings Mean for Plant-Based Diets.

The discovery of fungal toxins in all 212 products highlights the importance of studying dietary exposure across multiple foods, rather than evaluating each product in isolation.

In a recent development, for consumers, the results are not a reason to abandon vegan or vegetarian foods. The concentrations measured were below recommended EU guidelines, and the researchers stress that mycotoxins cannot be completely eliminated from the food supply.

Sources indicate that instead, the study points to the need for continued research into how different eating habits influence exposure, particularly among people who depend heavily on plant-based products. The University of Parma and Cranfield University are continuing their collaboration to investigate these dietary patterns, identify potentially vulnerable groups, and provide evidence that can inform future food safety policies.

The research, titled "Mycotoxin contamination in plant-based beverages and meat alternatives: A survey of the UK market," was published in the journal Food Control.

The study was conducted as part of the European Union-funded Horizon Europe FunShield4Med project (HORIZON-WIDERA-2021-ACCESS-03), Grant Agreement No 101079173.

Materials provided by Cranfield University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Scotland face a two-legged World Cup qualifying play-off against powerhouses Sweden, who are managed by Andreatta's former boss Tony Gustavsson.

The Swedes, who have been semi-finalists at the two previous Women's World Cups and are ranked eighth in the world, will be strong favourites to reach the tournament in Brazil next summer.

Andreatta, who has eight wins, two losses and four draws from her 14 games in charge of Scotland, was Gustavsson's deputy when he was Australia head coach from 2020 to 2024.

While the two have a connection from those years, the Australian is very much in business mode with next week's first leg at St Mirren Park looming.

"A few weeks ago Tony reached out, sent me a few messages and I took my time to respond," she told BBC Scotland.

"It wasn't much about football, just connecting on a personal level - which is probably a good thing, because I can be quite competitive. I just want to focus on business and not the personal level.

"I'm sure, like he is, all we're focused on is how we're going to win.".

Listen to the full interview with Melissa Andreatta.

The Scots finished top of their qualifying group earlier this year after four wins from their six games before beating the Czech Republic 5-2 on aggregate in the play-off semi-final.

That set up the exacting play-off final against the Swedes, a team who narrowly missed out on a spot in the final at the previous two World Cups.

Scotland have made just one appearance at the tournament, in 2019, and Andreatta is excited by the prospect of getting one over her old boss for her new home.

"It's going to be a great occasion to face them at home first," she added.

"They are such a powerhouse nation that carries so much expectation to go to their next tournament. We want to bring that all crashing down and do that in a truly Scottish way. That's what we're going to focus on.

"I definitely won't be looking at their dug out, I'll be focused on us and what we need to do to get the result and go to another tournament.

"They are an exceptional team but we won't be swayed by a team's reputation or ranking.

Recent findings suggest that "We firmly believe that anything is possible. Once that whistle goes, if you've done the work and you're prepared you're in the position to make anything happen. With this group of players and staff I know that's possible, we can take it to anyone on any given day.

Recent findings suggest that "It is a massive challenge but we love those moments and that's why we're here. We've earned it.".

Melissa Andreatta with daughter Mackenzie after Scotland beat the Czech Republic in their World Cup qualification semi-final.

There are more than 10,000 miles between Brisbane - where Andreatta grew up - and Ayr in Scotland, where she now calls home.

While the climate may be vastly different, there's one thing they do have in common - the beach.

Recent findings suggest that "I love the coastal life. In Australia it's a substantial part of your lifestyle, being outdoors. I think there's something about the sea, being near it. Relaxing, calming, balancing," she remarked.

It has been 18 months since Andreatta was announced as Pedro Martinez Losa's successor as manager of the Scotland women's team and now, with her family alongside her - including two-year-old daughter Mackenzie - she feels at home.

Sources indicate that "We've definitely settled in," she added. "We have the spots that we go to, our routine, we love it here. It's been a great landing spot for us on such a big move.".

But what does her daughter make of her mum's job?

It has been revealed that "She's got no idea," states Andreatta. "She just think's mum's on TV. Whenever she sees me she gets excited. Having her at the games is super special, being able to hold her on the pitch. She's such a joy.

"You do these things to make people proud and I want to make her proud.".

Andreatta has made a promising start as Scotland manager - but now faces a huge task.

Scotland without captain Weir for World Cup play-off.

New strategy rolled out to transform Scottish women's football over 10 years.

Andreatta was sitting in the pubs of Scotland over the summer as the Tartan Army headed over to the United States in their droves to watch the men's team compete at a first World Cup in almost 30 years.

The women won't have to wait that long if they can book a spot on the plane to Brazil next summer.

Andreatta is hoping to see just as many kilts on the Copacabana beach as there were in the bars of Boston.

"There is a strong desire among the group, not only players but also the staff, there is this desire to make their nation proud and show Scotland that the women's national team belongs here and deserves as much of the limelight as the men's," she added.

Recent findings suggest that "Together we can make our nation proud and what better way to do it? To have our men at the World Cup and then the following summer our women.

Tech Report: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (965 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky.
  • Recent findings suggest that putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine.
  • Sources indicate that in July, Russia announced that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky. According to Putin, Russia has control of the city in the Donbas; the remaining civilian population, he says, could be evacuated. It would take five days to clear the access roads. The Russian leader has suggested that human rights organizations from Ukraine and Russia and delegates from the foreign press be incorporated into the mission.

Recent findings suggest that putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine. Experts say that while Russia is indicating a readiness to make agreements, at the same time it is propagating its own depiction of the situation on the front line.

Sources indicate that in July, Russia announced that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof. Ukraine states the fighting there is still ongoing. Experts from the Ukrainian open-source interactive map of military operations project DeepState say that the city is still controlled by the Ukrainian army, but that the situation there is "extremely difficult.".

Responding to the proposal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told journalists: "Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city." He emphasized that Ukraine had always given the civilian population in Kostiantynivka opportunities to leave, and stated that Russia had used the temporary ceasefire in Oleshky to bring military equipment and weapons into the city.

Kostiantynivka is the southernmost city in the so-called Donetsk "fortress belt," which also includes Druzhkivka, Kramatorsk and Sloviansk. Taking Kostiantynivka would open the way for Russian troops to advance to Druzhkivka, and on to the conurbation of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk.

Oleksandr Kovalenko, a military expert at the Dmytro Tymchuk Center for Security Studies, a Ukrainian think tank, noted Kostiantynivka's role is similar to that of Bakhmut, Avdiivka or Chasiv Yar — towns whose defensive installations were able to hold back Russian enemy forces for years.

Industry observers note that local authorities say the humanitarian situation in the city, whose population before the start of Russia's full-scale invasion was around 70,000, is catastrophic and that some 340 civilians remain. They add thatKostiantynivkahas no central water, electricity or gas supplies, there is no public transport, and since the spring of 2026 people have only been able to evacuate on foot.

According to recent reports, "Those who stayed in Kostiantynivka need to be evacuated, they need a chance of a better life," military analyst Denys Popovych told DW. However, he added that an evacuation was virtually impossible without a ceasefire, as Russian troops had occupied the road between the town and Druzhkivka and drones were being deployed throughout the region. Ukraine, therefore, could not carry out such an operation unilaterally. "It still takes two to tango — to evacuate the people, that is," he mentioned.

It has been revealed that kovalenko believes that Moscow is simply using the humanitarian issue for purposes of manipulation and to strengthen its negotiating position. The Russian army, he stated, wants to gain time in order to reinforce units fighting in the vicinity.

It has been revealed that yevhen Zakharov, the director of the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group, has similar concerns. "I'm afraid that this proposal by the Russians has very different objectives to those they claim to pursue," he told DW. He described Putin's initiative as suspect, and noted the Ukrainian side should treat it with the utmost caution.

Industry observers note that kyiv is in a difficult position, as the idea of a mission for Kostiantynivka is also being pushed by US intermediaries. "If we reject it, they'll say to us: 'You're rejecting peace proposals, you're not taking care of your own citizens, why should we keep talking to you, Zelenskyy wants to continue the war.' This is precisely the calculation behind it all," noted Popovych.

After the end of the ceasefire in Oleshky, which was in place from October 27 to November 1, the Ukrainian General Staff announced that, in that time, the Russians had rotated their troops, entrenched their positions, reinforced measures to repel drones and brought in ammunition.

Kovalenko is convinced that the reason Russia is proposing a ceasefire is because its army is gradually losing ground in Kostiantynivka. From Moscow's perspective, the Russian troops that are meant to be storming the city are in urgent need of reinforcements, which they can't get because of the fighting on the ground.

"If a so-called humanitarian mission were to take place in Kostiantynivka, it would be a disaster for Kyiv, because Russia would use that time to consolidate forces that would enable it to take the city," he warned.

Popovych, however, does not think Ukraine should reject the Russian proposal. In his view, Kyiv should base its tactics on experiences with previous ceasefires and insist on very clear conditions in advance. "If there is a ceasefire, soldiers currently at their posts should stay there and not move," he suggested.

Oleksandr Pavlichenko from the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union believes Ukraine should submit a counter-proposal, which envisages the withdrawal of Russian troops from the Ukrainian city and the unimpeded departure of the civilian population.

It has been revealed that the human rights activist said that, for a genuine humanitarian mission to be put in place, a strong, neutral third party should be brought in to supervise and ensure safe passage. In his view, the only party with such a mandate is the International Committee of the Red Cross. "If a proposal comes from only one side, and from a side such as Russia, it doesn't inspire confidence," he said.

This article was originally written in Ukrainian.
